codingProjects.name: Coding & Programming
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Design and develop a standalone computer application that solves a specific problem or completes a defined task. Your finished program should demonstrate logical thinking, technical skill, creativity, and thoughtful software development. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete, working standalone application based on the current FBLA event topic. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Identify the problem your application is designed to solve. • Plan the program before development begins. • Write functional code that accomplishes the required task. • Test the program and correct errors. • Make thoughtful choices about program structure, usability, and design. • Be prepared to explain important coding decisions and how your program works. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Programming, debugging, problem-solving, logical thinking, software design, testing, documentation, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A completed working program and a presentation explaining the purpose of the application, how it works, major features, development decisions, problems you encountered, and how you solved them. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Coding & Programming Event Details & Guidelines to create a requirements checklist in your README. Turn the major requirements into project milestones. Use your GitHub repository to document development, commits, testing, revisions, and progress throughout the project.

codingProjects.name: Computer Game & Simulation Programming
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Design and develop an interactive computer game or simulation based on the current FBLA topic. The project should demonstrate programming skill, creativity, logical thinking, and effective interaction with the user. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete, functional game or simulation that responds to user actions and fulfills the assigned topic or purpose. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Define the purpose, objective, or problem represented by the game or simulation. • Plan the rules, interactions, user controls, and overall flow. • Program the major features and interactive elements. • Provide clear instructions for the user. • Test the program for errors, usability, and proper operation. • Refine the program based on testing and feedback. • Be prepared to explain both the programming and design decisions behind the project. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Programming, game or simulation design, algorithms, debugging, user-interface design, problem-solving, testing, creativity, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A working game or simulation and a presentation demonstrating how it works, how users interact with it, how it addresses the FBLA topic, and how it was designed and developed. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Computer Game & Simulation Programming Event Details & Guidelines to build your README requirements checklist. Break development into milestones such as planning, prototype creation, programming major features, testing, revisions, and final presentation preparation. Document your progress and revisions in GitHub.

codingProjects.name: Data Analysis
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Examine and interpret a provided data set to discover meaningful patterns, trends, relationships, or insights that can support decision-making. Your project should show that you can move from raw data to understandable conclusions. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete data analysis supported by appropriate charts, graphs, tables, dashboards, or other visualizations. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Understand the question or problem represented by the data. • Examine and organize the provided data set. • Identify important patterns, trends, relationships, or unusual results. • Select appropriate methods for analyzing the data. • Create clear and accurate data visualizations. • Explain what the results mean rather than simply displaying numbers. • Develop conclusions or recommendations supported by evidence from the data. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Data analysis, spreadsheets or programming tools, statistics, data visualization, critical thinking, interpretation, communication, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT Your analysis, visualizations, conclusions, and a presentation explaining what you discovered and how the information could support a decision or solve a problem. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Data Analysis Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Build milestones for data review, cleaning or organization, analysis, visualization, interpretation, revision, and presentation preparation. Keep evidence of your analysis process and revisions in your project repository.

codingProjects.name: Introduction to Programming
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW 9th and 10th grade only. Design and develop a basic computer program based on the current FBLA topic. The project should demonstrate your ability to use programming concepts, logical thinking, and creativity to solve a defined problem. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete working computer program based on the assigned FBLA topic. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Understand the problem or task described by the event topic. • Plan the program before writing the final code. • Use appropriate programming concepts to create the solution. • Make the program functional and easy to understand or use. • Test the program and correct errors. • Be prepared to demonstrate the program and explain how the code works. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Beginning programming, logic, debugging, problem-solving, planning, testing, communication, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A working program and a presentation demonstrating its major features and explaining how your code and design address the assigned topic. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Introduction to Programming Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Break the project into manageable milestones such as planning, first prototype, coding, testing, revision, and final presentation. Use GitHub to document your progress.

codingProjects.name: Mobile Application Development
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Design and develop a functional mobile application based on the current FBLA topic. The app should demonstrate useful functionality, thoughtful interface design, creativity, and technical problem-solving. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A working mobile application designed for a specific purpose and user audience. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Identify the app's purpose and intended users. • Plan the screens, navigation, features, and user interactions. • Build the major required functions of the application. • Create a clear and usable interface. • Test navigation, features, and user interactions. • Correct technical problems and improve usability. • Be prepared to explain the design and development choices you made. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Mobile programming, user-interface design, navigation design, debugging, problem-solving, testing, creativity, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A functional mobile application and a presentation demonstrating its features, intended audience, interface, technical development, and connection to the FBLA topic. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Mobile Application Development Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Develop milestones for planning, interface design, prototype development, programming, testing, revision, and final presentation. Document your progress and major development decisions in GitHub.

codingProjects.name: Website Coding & Development
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Design and build a functioning website based on the current FBLA topic, with an emphasis on coding, technical functionality, and web-development problem-solving rather than appearance alone. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete working website that includes meaningful functionality and demonstrates web-development skills. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Determine the purpose and intended audience of the site. • Plan the site's structure, pages, navigation, and technical features. • Develop the site using appropriate web technologies. • Create functional features rather than relying only on static design. • Make navigation and interaction clear for the user. • Test links, features, responsiveness, and usability. • Debug problems and refine the finished website. • Be prepared to explain your code and technical decisions. SKILLS YOU WILL USE HTML, CSS, JavaScript or other web technologies, debugging, responsive design, problem-solving, testing, user experience, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A working website and a presentation demonstrating its functionality, technical features, development process, and how it addresses the assigned FBLA topic. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Website Coding & Development Event Details & Guidelines to build your README checklist. Create milestones for planning, site structure, initial coding, feature development, testing, revisions, deployment, and presentation preparation. Track your development through GitHub commits.

codingProjects.name: Website Design
codingProjects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Create a visually engaging, user-friendly website based on the current FBLA topic. This event emphasizes front-end design, layout, navigation, aesthetics, accessibility, and the overall user experience. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete website designed for a specific audience and purpose. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Identify the purpose and target audience for the site. • Plan the page structure and navigation. • Create a consistent visual theme. • Use effective typography, color, imagery, spacing, and layout. • Make navigation clear and intuitive. • Design for usability and accessibility. • Test the site on different screen sizes when appropriate. • Revise the design based on testing and feedback. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Web design, HTML and CSS, layout, typography, color theory, usability, accessibility, responsive design, creativity, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A completed website and a presentation explaining the target audience, design choices, navigation, user experience, and how the site addresses the assigned topic. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Website Design Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Develop milestones for research, wireframes or planning, first design, page development, usability testing, revisions, and final presentation. Use GitHub to document the evolution of the site.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Business Plan
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Develop a comprehensive plan for launching a new business. Your project should show that you understand how a business idea can be researched, organized, financed, marketed, and operated successfully. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete written business plan and a presentation explaining the proposed business. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Clearly describe the business concept, product, or service. • Identify the target customer and market need. • Research competitors and explain your competitive advantage. • Develop a marketing and sales strategy. • Explain how the business will operate. • Address staffing, management, or organizational needs where appropriate. • Develop realistic financial information and projections. • Use research and evidence to support your decisions. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Business planning, market research, financial planning, entrepreneurship, writing, organization, critical thinking, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A pre-judged written business plan and a live presentation explaining the business concept and why the proposed business could succeed. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Business Plan Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Break the report into milestones such as concept development, market research, marketing plan, operations, financial planning, written report revision, and presentation preparation. Keep your research sources and project revisions organized as evidence of your work.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Event Planning
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Develop and present a detailed plan for a real event based on the assigned FBLA topic. Your plan should demonstrate that you understand the organization, budgeting, promotion, scheduling, logistics, and problem-solving required to manage an event successfully. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete event plan that could realistically be used to organize and conduct the proposed event. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Define the purpose, goals, and target audience for the event. • Select an appropriate location or format. • Develop a schedule or timeline. • Create a realistic budget. • Plan marketing and promotion. • Address staffing, vendors, equipment, supplies, and other logistics. • Consider safety, accessibility, risks, and possible problems. • Explain how you would evaluate whether the event was successful. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Project management, budgeting, scheduling, marketing, organization, logistics, communication, problem-solving, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A detailed event plan and a live presentation explaining how the event would be organized and successfully carried out. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Event Planning Event Details & Guidelines to build your README checklist. Create milestones for research, event concept, budget, schedule, promotion, logistics, contingency planning, revisions, and presentation preparation. Keep evidence of planning changes and decisions as your project develops.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Introduction to Business Presentation
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW 9th and 10th grade only. Develop and deliver a professional business-focused presentation based on the assigned FBLA topic, using presentation software as an effective visual aid. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A polished business presentation supported by professional visual slides or other approved presentation media. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Understand and address the assigned business topic. • Research the information needed for the presentation. • Organize ideas in a clear and logical sequence. • Create professional visual aids that support rather than overwhelm the message. • Use appropriate business vocabulary and examples. • Practice clear, confident delivery. • Be prepared to answer questions or explain your ideas when required. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Research, business communication, organization, slide design, visual communication, public speaking, critical thinking, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A live business presentation supported by presentation software or other required visual materials. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Introduction to Business Presentation Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Develop milestones for topic research, outline creation, slide development, revision, rehearsal, and final presentation preparation. Save drafts and revisions as evidence of your progress.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Introduction to Social Media Strategy
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW 9th and 10th grade only. Develop and present a social media strategy centered around one social media platform. Your strategy should demonstrate an understanding of the audience, content, engagement, branding, and campaign effectiveness. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete social media strategy for the assigned FBLA topic using one selected social media platform. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Identify the organization, purpose, or campaign goal. • Define the target audience. • Select an appropriate social media platform and explain why it fits the audience. • Develop a consistent message and brand approach. • Plan appropriate content and posting ideas. • Explain how the organization would engage with its audience. • Identify useful metrics for measuring campaign effectiveness. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Marketing, audience analysis, social media planning, branding, content creation, communication, analytics, creativity, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A complete strategy and a live presentation explaining the platform choice, audience, content plan, engagement approach, and how success would be measured. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Introduction to Social Media Strategy Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Develop milestones for audience research, platform selection, branding, content planning, sample content, metrics, revision, and presentation preparation. Keep evidence of your research and strategy development.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Sales Presentation
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Create and deliver an interactive sales presentation for a product or service of your choice. Your goal is to demonstrate that you can identify customer needs, communicate value, respond professionally, and persuade a potential customer. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete sales presentation designed around a specific product or service and a clearly defined customer. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Know the product or service thoroughly. • Identify the target customer and likely customer needs. • Develop a clear opening and sales approach. • Explain important features and translate them into customer benefits. • Use evidence, examples, demonstrations, or visuals when appropriate. • Anticipate possible customer concerns or objections. • Develop professional responses to those concerns. • End with an appropriate closing or call to action. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Sales, communication, persuasion, product research, audience analysis, listening, problem-solving, professionalism, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT An interactive live sales presentation demonstrating product knowledge, persuasive communication, customer engagement, and effective sales techniques. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Sales Presentation Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Develop milestones for product research, customer analysis, sales script or outline, visuals or demonstration materials, objection handling, rehearsal, revision, and final presentation.

businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.name: Social Media Strategies
businessMarketingEntrepreneurship.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Develop and present a comprehensive marketing campaign that uses multiple social media platforms. The campaign should demonstrate strategic planning, consistent branding, audience engagement, content creation, and the ability to evaluate campaign performance. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete multi-platform social media marketing strategy based on the assigned FBLA topic. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Identify campaign goals and the target audience. • Select appropriate social media platforms for the audience and purpose. • Develop a consistent brand voice, message, and visual identity. • Plan platform-appropriate content. • Show how content will work together across multiple platforms. • Develop strategies for audience engagement and interaction. • Identify metrics or analytics that would measure performance. • Explain how the strategy could be adjusted based on results. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Digital marketing, branding, content strategy, audience analysis, communication, analytics, creativity, campaign planning, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A comprehensive social media campaign strategy and a presentation explaining the campaign goals, target audience, platform choices, content plan, branding, engagement strategy, and measurement methods. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Social Media Strategies Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Build milestones for audience research, platform planning, branding, content development, sample posts, engagement strategy, analytics, revisions, and presentation preparation.

graphicDesign.name: Digital Animation
graphicDesign.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Design and produce an original animated video based on the assigned FBLA topic. Your animation should demonstrate creativity, storytelling, technical ability, and an understanding of animation principles. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete original animated video that clearly communicates the assigned topic or message. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Interpret the event topic and identify the intended audience. • Develop a concept, script, storyboard, or other production plan. • Create original animated content. • Apply appropriate animation principles and techniques. • Use visual design, timing, movement, sound, and storytelling effectively. • Edit and refine the finished animation. • Be prepared to explain the creative and technical process used to produce it. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Animation, storyboarding, visual design, storytelling, editing, digital media tools, creativity, technical problem-solving, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A pre-judged animated video and a live presentation explaining the concept, development process, tools, creative choices, challenges, revisions, and finished product. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Digital Animation Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Develop milestones for concept development, storyboard or planning, asset creation, first animation draft, editing, feedback, revisions, final export, and presentation preparation. Save evidence of your creative process and revisions.

graphicDesign.name: Digital Video Production
graphicDesign.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Plan, record, edit, and produce an original digital video based on the assigned FBLA topic and intended audience. Your project should demonstrate effective storytelling, strong production quality, creativity, and purposeful communication. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete original video designed to communicate a clear message to a specific audience. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Interpret the topic and define the intended audience and purpose. • Develop a concept, script, storyboard, or shot plan. • Plan locations, equipment, performers, graphics, audio, and other production needs. • Record original video and audio content as required. • Edit footage into a clear, professional final production. • Use audio, graphics, transitions, pacing, and visual effects appropriately. • Review and revise the video for technical and communication quality. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Video planning, scriptwriting, recording, editing, audio production, visual communication, storytelling, creativity, project management, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A pre-judged finished video and a live presentation explaining the purpose, target audience, production process, creative choices, tools, challenges, revisions, and final result. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Digital Video Production Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Develop milestones for research, script or storyboard, production planning, recording, first edit, feedback, revisions, final export, and presentation preparation. Preserve drafts and production evidence as part of your project documentation.

graphicDesign.name: Graphic Design
graphicDesign.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Create original visual materials based on the assigned FBLA topic. Your work should demonstrate effective visual communication, creativity, technical skill, and thoughtful use of design principles and digital tools. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A coordinated set of original graphic-design materials that communicate a clear message to the intended audience. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Understand the topic, purpose, and intended audience. • Research appropriate design styles and communication needs. • Develop original concepts and rough ideas before creating the final design. • Apply design principles such as balance, contrast, alignment, hierarchy, repetition, and proximity. • Use typography, color, imagery, and layout intentionally. • Maintain visual consistency across the required materials. • Revise designs based on feedback and evaluation. • Be prepared to explain the creative process and design decisions. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Graphic design, typography, color theory, layout, branding, visual communication, digital design software, creativity, revision, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT The required original design materials and a presentation explaining the purpose, audience, design process, tools, visual choices, revisions, and final results. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Graphic Design Event Details & Guidelines to build your README checklist. Develop milestones for research, brainstorming, sketches or drafts, first digital designs, feedback, revision, final exports, and presentation preparation. Keep drafts and revisions to show how the design evolved.

graphicDesign.name: Public Service Announcement
graphicDesign.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Create an original 60-second public service announcement that raises awareness about the assigned issue and encourages the audience to think, respond, or take action. The project should combine research, clear messaging, creativity, and effective video production. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE A complete 60-second original PSA video based on the assigned FBLA topic. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Research the issue and understand the facts behind the message. • Identify the target audience. • Define the main objective or action you want the audience to take. • Develop a clear, focused message. • Plan the PSA using a script, storyboard, or production outline. • Create or obtain appropriate visuals and audio according to event rules. • Edit the production so the message is understandable, engaging, and persuasive. • Be prepared to explain the research, creative choices, and production process. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Research, persuasive communication, scriptwriting, video production, editing, audience analysis, storytelling, creativity, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT A completed 60-second PSA and a live presentation explaining the issue, target audience, communication objective, creative process, production decisions, and intended impact. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Public Service Announcement Event Details & Guidelines to create your README checklist. Build milestones for research, message development, script or storyboard, recording, editing, review, revision, final export, and presentation preparation. Keep evidence of drafts and revisions.

graphicDesign.name: Visual Design
graphicDesign.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW Develop original visual content based on the assigned FBLA topic. Your project should demonstrate creativity, effective visual communication, strong design principles, and a clear connection between the finished materials and their intended purpose. WHAT YOU WILL CREATE The complete set of visual materials required by the current FBLA event topic. MAJOR REQUIREMENTS • Understand the event topic, purpose, and intended audience. • Identify every visual item required by the official guidelines. • Develop concepts through brainstorming, sketches, or drafts. • Apply design principles such as balance, contrast, alignment, hierarchy, repetition, and proximity. • Use typography, color, imagery, and layout intentionally. • Keep the different materials visually consistent with one another and with the theme. • Revise and refine the designs based on evaluation and feedback. • Explain how the creative process moved from initial ideas to final designs. SKILLS YOU WILL USE Visual design, graphic design, typography, color theory, layout, branding, creative problem-solving, digital design software, revision, and presentation skills. WHAT YOU WILL PRESENT OR SUBMIT The required visual materials and a presentation explaining the topic, intended audience, design principles, creative process, tools, revisions, challenges, and final design decisions. WBL PLANNING Use the official FBLA Visual Design Event Details & Guidelines to create your README requirements checklist. Make sure every required visual item appears on that checklist. Develop milestones for research, brainstorming, drafts, digital development, feedback, revisions, final exports, and presentation preparation. Keep early versions so you can demonstrate how your designs changed over time.
